datasets.name: HR Company
datasets.description: A small company with employees, departments and salary records.
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE departments (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, location VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE employees (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, department_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES departments(id), hire_date DATE NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE salaries (employee_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES employees(id), amount INT NOT NULL, effective_date DATE NOT NULL)

datasets.name: Retail Store
datasets.description: An online store with customers, products and orders.
schemaSql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, city VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE products (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL, category VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, price INT NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE orders (id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(id), product_id INT NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id), quantity INT NOT NULL, order_date DATE NOT NULL, total INT NOT NULL)

questions.question: List the name and hire date of every employee.
questions.hint: Select two columns from the employees table.

questions.question: Find employees hired on or after 2022-01-01 (name and hire date).
questions.hint: Filter hire_date with a WHERE clause.
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT name, hire_date FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= DATE '2022-01-01'

questions.question: Show each employee's name together with their department name.
questions.hint: Join employees to departments on department_id.
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT e.name AS employee, d.name AS department FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id

questions.question: Count the number of employees in each department (department name and count).
questions.hint: GROUP BY department and use COUNT(*).
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name

questions.question: List departments that have more than one employee (department name and count).
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

questions.question: Find the second highest salary amount.
questions.hint: Find the maximum salary that is lower than the overall maximum.
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT MAX(amount) AS salary FROM salaries WHERE amount < (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM salaries)

questions.question: Using a CTE, find the average salary in each department (department name and average).
questions.hint: Start with WITH dept_salary AS (...) and then aggregate.
questions.referenceQuery: WITH dept_salary AS (SELECT e.department_id, s.amount FROM employees e JOIN salaries s ON s.employee_id = e.id) SELECT d.name AS department, AVG(ds.amount) AS avg_salary FROM dept_salary ds JOIN departments d ON d.id = ds.department_id GROUP BY d.name

questions.question: Rank employees by salary within each department (name, department, salary, rank).
questions.hint: Use RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY amount DESC).
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department, s.amount AS salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY s.amount DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN salaries s ON s.employee_id = e.id

questions.question: List the name and price of every product.
questions.hint: Select two columns from the products table.

questions.question: Find Electronics products priced above ₹5,000 (name and price).
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' AND price > 5000

questions.question: Show every order ID with the customer's name.
questions.hint: Join orders to customers on customer_id.
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id

questions.question: Calculate the total order value for each city (city and total).
questions.hint: Join orders to customers, then GROUP BY city with SUM(total).
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT c.city, SUM(o.total) AS total_value FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city

questions.question: List customers who placed more than one order (customer name and order count).
questions.hint: GROUP BY customer and filter with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT c.name AS customer, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

questions.question: Find products priced above the average product price (name and price).
questions.hint: Compare price with (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products).
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products)

questions.question: Using a CTE, find the customer with the highest total spend (customer name and total).
questions.hint: Aggregate spend per customer in a CTE, then order by it.
questions.referenceQuery: WITH spend AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total) AS total_spend FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT c.name AS customer, s.total_spend FROM spend s JOIN customers c ON c.id = s.customer_id ORDER BY s.total_spend DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: Show a running total of order value by order date (order date, total, running total), ordered by date.
questions.referenceQuery: SELECT order_date, total, SUM(total) OVER (ORDER BY order_date) AS running_total FROM orders ORDER BY order_date
